25. OBESITY IN PREGNANCY
•21% pregnant population is obese
•47% have normal BMI.

Maternal Risk:

•GDM
•HTN.
•VTE.
•PE.
•Labor:
-IOL.
-Dysfunctional labour
-Prolonged labour
•C/S.
•Anesthetic complication.
•Maternal mortality and morbidity (30% obese and 22% over weight)

Fetal:

•Miscarriages
•Anomalies (obese + GDM 3x anomalies).
•Macrosomia. BMI Classification:
•Still birth. 1. Underweight <18.5
•Pre – maturity. 2. Normal 18.5-24.9
•Neonatal death. 3. Overweight > 25

4. Pre-obese 25-29.9

5. Class I 30-34.9

6. Class II 35-39.9

7. Class III 40 and above.

Pre – pregnancy:

•Weight reduction if BMI is > 30.
•Weight reduces (1) still birth (2), HTN (3), macrosomia.
•VBAC success
•5mg FA 1-month pre – pregnancy if BMI > 30.
•Vitamin D, 10ug (1000IU) daily.

ANC:

MDT:

•Consultant led BMI>35.
•Facilities and equipment BMI >30.
•Assessment of BMI @ booking then 3rd to make appropriate plan for equipment and personal required during labour and birth.
•Weight gain – no consensus.
•Dietary advice by trained professional.
•Anti – obesity drugs.
1.Orlistat – congenital anomalies.

Suppress

2.Topiramate – oral cleft. appetite
3.Phentermine – oral cleft
4.Lorcaserin HT2C promote satiety.
•Anesthetic assessment by obstetric anesthetist if BMI > 40.
•Pressure sore BMI >40.

BMI & THEIR IMPLICATIONS:

BMI 40 & More:

•Anaesthesia evaluation.
•Uterine rupture.
•Pressure sores.
•I/V line in labour.
•Higher loss rate with amniocentesis.

BMI 35 & Above:

•HTN, pre-eclampsia.
•Difficult to measure SFH.
•Post-dated.
•Still birth.
•Consultant led care.

BMI 30 & Above:

•GDM screening.
•VTE, risk assessment/ scoring.
•Mental health screening.
•Wound infection.
•Pre – pregnancy counselling.
•Folic acid.
•Vitamin D levels.
•Lactation advice.
•GDM Screening BMI > 30.
•HTN Screening:
-Proper sized cuff.
⇨Std – 12 x 23cms.
⇨Large – 15 x 33.
⇨Thigh – 18 x 30.
-B.P @ all visits.
-P.E more in class II.
-BMI > 35 aspirin 150mg from 12 weeks till birth + 1 another moderate risk factor.
•Mental health screening:
-BMI > 30 Risk – so do screening of mental health in antenatal period

A/N depression:

-Obese – 33%.
-Over weight – 28%.
-(N) weight – 22%.

P/N depression:

-Obese – 13%.
-Over weight – 11%.
-(N) weight – 9%.
•Chromosomal screening:
-TVS for NT (if difficult TAS)
-NiPT non – specific.
-Invasive procedure doesn’t risk of miscarriages in BMI 30 – 40
-Loss rate in BMI > 48%.
•Structural Screening:
-Difficult in obese
•Fetal monitoring:
-SFH – after 24 hours to assess growth routinely.
-SFH – difficult after BMI 35 so assess by USG.
-USG for fetal presentation.
-FHR by pinard stethoscope/ Doppler USG.
-Risk of postdates and still birth BMI > 35 after 37 weeks.

•Labour Planning:
-MDT:
⇨Midwife.
⇨Obstetrician
⇨Anaesthetist.
-Multiparous low risk in Midwifery led unit.
-Active management of 3rd stage.

 

-IOL chances of LSCS and macrosomia.

Elective induction @ 37 weeks or after 37 weeks on individual basis.

-LSCS due to obesity => MDT.

C/S in obese – 50%.

-Macrosomia – consider IOL.

NICE:

-BMI >35 – Consultant led unit.
-30 – 35 – individualized management.

VBAC:

•BMI > 30 – individualized plan (54% success of VBAC in obese, 70% in (N) BMI).
•Class III obesity – risk of rapture.

IPC:

•Class I, II not an indication for CLU.

Informed choice of women either MLU/ CLU.

•Class III continuous midwife care.
•BMI >40 I/V line.

LSCS:

-Individualized circumstances
- scar on skin.
-Supra pannus transverse.
-Supra Pannus vertical

Supra pannus scars increase chances of blood loss, Pain, respiratory morbidity.

Risk of infection not known.

Wound infection > BMI 30 – prophylactic A/B.

•Negative pressure dressing.
•> 2cm Fat => stretching to reduce infection.

PNC:

•Breast feeding > 30 => appropriate specialist advice.
•Weight reduction support.

B.F in obesity:

-Delay lactogenesis – impaired prolactin response to suckling.
-Lower initiation.
-Earlier cessation.
•Dietary advice by trained professional.
•Referral to weight loss management services.

Bariatric Surgery:

•C/C for 12 – 18m0 after surgery.
•CLU as it is high risk.
•Nutritional surveillance/ screening:
-Iron.
-Folate. Micro – nutritional
-B – 12.
-Fat soluble.
-Vitamins.
-Fats. Macro – nutritional
-Proteins.

 

Anaesthesia Complication in Obese Women:

•Cardiac arrest 25% due to anaesthesia.

75 % in obese.

•Difficult intubation.
•Higher de-saturation.
•Induction and recovery time.
